Subject: Re: Onramp: VPC LogRelay + scrub-proxy (initial ask)

Hi Tom — thanks, and good call. High level plan attached and an evidence checklist (see attachments). TL;DR: scrub-proxy can run in either the transit VPC or the inference subnet, but there are tradeoffs:

- Transit VPC (recommended for AcmeCloud): easier multi-team ownership and less blast radius on inference hosts. Requires a secure tunnel (mTLS) and strict egress ACLs from the scrub-proxy to Redwood's LogRelay endpoint.
- Inference subnet colocated: lower hop count and slightly lower latency for log delivery, but increases host-level attack surface and complicates host patching ownership.

We need the following from your side to complete the security package:
1) Splunk HEC endpoint (or a Splunk-to-Redwood broker plan) and any token rotation cadence.
2) Network egress policy for the scrub-proxy (CIDR ranges) and whether your transit VPC allows outbound mTLS to our IP ranges.
3) A sample redacted log set (1–2MB) so we can validate scrub rules.

Action items:
- Kimberly: can you confirm minimum encryption and token rotation expectations for our evidence checklist?
- Jonas: I'll need a short runbook you can sign off on for deploy/rollback.

Tom — attaching: scrub-proxy-config-v1.yaml (example), evidence-handshake-checklist.pdf, splunk-hec-guidance.docx. I can hop on a 30m call later today if helpful.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Observability Partnerships
Redwood Inference

On Sat, Jul 20, 2029 at 11:02 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We need the following from your side to complete the security package:
> 1) Splunk HEC endpoint...

Quick technical notes from my side (deploy/rollback runbook + constraints):

- Deploy topology we recommend for Acme: two scrub-proxy replicas in transit VPC across AZs, route logs to a central LogRelay NATed egress with enforced mTLS. Use our provided client certs; we'll rotate certs quarterly.
- Scrubbing: prefer in-proxy filtering + structural redaction for JSON logs. Example rules in scrub-proxy-config-v1.yaml: mask_user_email, truncate-ssn, redact-raw-utterance.
- Backpressure / buffering: scrub-proxy must persist to local disk up to 200MB with LRU roll-off. If Splunk HEC is unavailable, LogRelay will accept retried deliveries from our side but we need the HEC consumer to support 429/backoff semantics.
- Rollback: switch route at transit VPC route table (remove routes to scrub-proxy subnets) + signal to LogRelay to drop the routing entry — full rollback window ~= 90s after route table change.

I'll draft the short runbook and post in the Drive link. Tom — can you share if Acme has any packet inspection that could break mTLS? If so, we'll need an alternate tunnel (IPsec) plan.

— Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Onramp: VPC LogRelay + scrub-proxy (initial ask)

Hi Tom — quick security checklist / clarifications (pulling from our SOC2 evidence expectations):

1) Evidence bundle: host inventory (AMI IDs / image hashes), scrub-proxy config (signed), TLS cert chain, ACLs (route table + NACL screenshots), and a short retention policy statement for logs that transit your scrub-proxy. We marked these in the attached evidence-handshake-checklist.pdf.
2) Token rotation: HEC tokens must rotate at least every 90 days; if you cannot rotate tokens that frequently, you must implement additional client-side signature (HMAC) that we can verify.
3) Access: only the scrub-proxy role should have write permission to the LogRelay egress group. Please provide RBAC screenshots or IAM policy snippets.
4) Splunk HEC: Kate, can you confirm if Splunk Cloud supports the persistent-backoff HTTP semantics Jonas mentioned? If not, we'll propose a buffer relay inside Redwood that temporarily accept logs and replay when Splunk recovers.

If you can push the ACL screenshots and a redacted host inventory by EOD 07/23 we should be in a good spot for your 07/29 review. We can run a 30m joint session to walk the checklist — Hannah, Jonas, Marissa, want to be on that call.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
